transcript.content: Hello and welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My mind feels foggy all the time—I can’t focus at work or even finish a simple puzzle like I used to. It's really starting to worry me, especially since it's affecting my ability to do my job as a security guard.
Along with this brain fog, have you also been feeling down, sad, or lost interest in the activities you usually enjoy?

Yes, I walk around with this heavy, empty sadness lately, and sometimes I even catch myself tearing up for no reason in the break room or driving home. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like cooking with my wife or playing guitar with my kid, and now I just sit on the couch staring at the TV.
Did you first notice the trouble with your concentration and memory, or did the feelings of sadness and loss of interest start before those mental changes?

Honestly, they both seemed to start around the same time, about three weeks ago. It all hit me during a really stressful, busy month at the casino when arguments with my wife were escalating. It’s hard to say which came first because they both just seemed to build up together.
Have you recently experienced any physical illnesses, head injuries, or been diagnosed with any new medical conditions around the time these symptoms started?

No, I haven't had any head injuries or physical illnesses recently. I also haven't been diagnosed with any new medical conditions around the time this all started. Aside from feeling completely drained, my physical health has been normal.
How has your sleep been lately? Have you had any trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or perhaps sleeping much more than usual?

My sleep is mostly just irregular because of my rotating night shifts at the casino. I haven't really noticed any major new problems with falling or staying asleep, other than my usual tiredness from the work schedule.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness, or feeling excessively guilty about things lately, even when they aren't your fault?
I haven't really been feeling worthless or excessively guilty. I do worry a lot about letting my family down or messing things up for them, though.
During this difficult time, have you had any thoughts of death, hurting yourself, or feeling like life is no longer worth living?

I don't have any plan to hurt myself, but I do get those thoughts sometimes. When I'm driving home after a long shift, I catch myself thinking it wouldn't really matter if I didn't wake up or if something happened to me. I just feel like my family might be better off without me messing things up.
How has your appetite been lately? Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since these symptoms started?

Most days I'm just not hungry, so I've been skipping meals at work or just picking at whatever is there. My wife has actually noticed that my work uniform is looking a bit looser around the waist lately.
Have you or your wife noticed if you are moving and speaking much slower than usual, or on the other hand, feeling very restless and unable to sit still?

Yes, my body feels like it's moving through mud lately. I'm much slower when walking my rounds at work, and even getting up from my chair in the control room takes an extra push. I don't feel restless at all; it's really just a heavy, physical slowness.
Have you ever experienced a period of low mood, sadness, or loss of interest like this at any other point in your life, or is this the very first time?
This is the very first time I've ever felt like this. I've never experienced this kind of heavy sadness or lost interest in my family and hobbies before now.
Do you feel this heavy sadness and loss of interest almost all day, nearly every day, or does your mood lift when you are away from work and things are calm at home?

I feel this heavy sadness almost all day, nearly every day, regardless of whether I'm at work or at home. Even on my nights off when things should be calm, I still feel empty and just go through the motions. I just don't have any desire to engage in the things I used to enjoy, no matter where I am.
Have you been using alcohol, recreational drugs, or any new medications since these symptoms started?
No, I haven't been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications since these symptoms started. I've just been trying to get through my shifts and my days at home on my own.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-episode depressive syndrome of 3 weeks' duration, characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue/decreased energy, impaired concentration, decreased appetite with weight loss, psychomotor retardation, and passive suicidal ideation (thoughts of death). The symptoms are pervasive, occurring nearly every day, and cause significant functional impairment at work and home. Although the onset coincided with psychosocial stressors (work stress and marital discord), the severity, number of symptoms, and pervasiveness of the depressive syndrome warrant a primary diagnosis of a depressive episode (F32) rather than an adjustment disorder (F43.2). There is no history of manic/hypomanic episodes or substance use contributing to the presentation.
